grammar_and_layout.method: Parsed all six complete UTF-8 files with Python ast.parse and raw web-tree-sitter using the installed WASM. Reproduced each with minimal source. The new parser throws when rootNode.hasError before Visitor.compile (parser.ts:80-86).

files.minimalTreeSitter: ERROR at 1:1 over the whole assignment
files.validPython: Unpacking a string in a tuple expression is valid; Python 3.13.13 ast.parse passes. A second minimal example g = 1, *[1, 2] also passes CPython and fails Tree-sitter.
files.rootCause: The Tree-sitter grammar aliases list_splat_pattern into primary_expression. list_splat_pattern permits only identifier, keyword_identifier, subscript, or attribute after *, not arbitrary expressions such as a string/list literal. The subsequent line-161 diagnostic is error recovery after line 160. *range(10) happens to parse as a call whose callee is *range, so that success is not general unpacking support.
files.repair: Allow list_splat (star plus full expression) in expression contexts; keep stricter assignment-target validation and verify Visitor maps the new node to DereferenceExpression. Regenerate the Python grammar WASM and check existing tuple unpacking cases.

files.validPython: PEP 696 default for TypeVarTuple, supported by Python 3.13.13; ast.parse passes. File also has **P defaults and class/function forms.
files.rootCause: type_parameter grammar is only [ commaSep1(type) ]; it has no = default clause for normal, *Ts, or **P type parameters. The full file has 8 ERROR nodes plus 1 missing ] node.
files.repair: Add type-parameter-default productions for TypeVar, TypeVarTuple, and ParamSpec, including expression and unpacked tuple defaults, then regenerate WASM. The current Visitor omits type_parameters; check whether parity only or preservation of defaults is required.

files.validPython: A parenthesized target inside a starred assignment target is valid; Python 3.13.13 ast.parse passes.
files.rootCause: list_splat_pattern permits only bare identifier, keyword_identifier, subscript, and attribute after *. It excludes parenthesized patterns. Because assignment LHS uses pattern/pattern_list, *(a) cannot match.
files.repair: Extend starred assignment-target grammar to accept parenthesized assignable targets, while retaining invalid-target rejection and checking Visitor output for parenthesized targets.

files.validPython: Parenthesized starred target in a list assignment is valid; Python 3.13.13 ast.parse passes.
files.rootCause: Same list_splat_pattern restriction as preview_unpacking_parens.py. Multiline layout changes where recovery reports the error; the missing grammar form is *(rest).
files.repair: Same grammar and Visitor work as the previous file, with a multiline regression case.

files.validPython: Type parameter defaults in type aliases are valid Python 3.13.13; ast.parse passes. This file contains T, *P, *Ts and unpacked defaults.
files.rootCause: Same type_parameter rule has no = default production. The first error is a plain T default; later cases include starred defaults. Raw Tree-sitter tree has 32 ERROR or MISSING nodes in full file.
files.repair: Implement PEP 696 defaults in grammar and regenerate WASM; check UAST parity after parse succeeds.

files.actualTrigger: lines 22-24: indented @property, flush-left comment-only line, indented def parent_attr
files.minimalTreeSitter: ERROR at 2:5 on "@property"; raw tree places decorator as ERROR child of class_definition while def remains in class block
files.validPython: Python 3.13.13 ast.parse passes: indentation of a comment-only line does not close the suite or detach the decorator.
files.rootCause: Tree-sitter Python 0.25.0 mishandles a column-zero comment between a decorator and its definition inside an indented suite. An indented comment at the same position parses; a column-zero comment between ordinary class statements parses. This localizes the problem to decorator/comment layout, likely grammar plus external scanner interaction. Exact scanner branch requires upstream debugging.
files.repair: Add a regression for flush-left comment-only lines between indented decorators and definitions. Adjust the grammar/scanner layout handling so such comments do not detach the decorator, then regenerate WASM. Avoid blindly reindenting source comments because offsets and original text matter.
